title: Athletics catcher Shea Langeliers placed on IL with torn meniscus
content:
Athletics catcher Shea Langeliers tore his meniscus, the team announced Sunday, placing him on the 10-day injured list retroactive to July 25. In the latest blow during a rough year for the last-place Athletics, Langeliers could miss the rest of the season.

The options for contending teams looking to bolster their catching position on the trade market were already thin before Langeliers’ injury. On the surface, Langeliers, 28, was a sensible trade target; a good player on a bad team. His trade outlook before the injury, however, contained some nuance; most notably, Langeliers is under club control through 2028, the year the Athletics expect to open their new $2 billion ballpark on the Las Vegas Strip, and a year in which they expect to contend.

Before the injury, Langeliers was unlikely to get traded, but some teams were hoping he’d nonetheless become more available.

Regardless, the injury takes him off the trade block. Langeliers, an All-Star, is hitting .263/.332/.497 with 23 home runs, while also being a top defensive catcher. With Langeliers out, the Athletics recalled catcher Brian Serven from Triple-A Las Vegas. Jonah Heim, another trade candidate, is set for the bulk of action in Langeliers’ place.

The Athletics (44-60) have lost seven of their last 10 games. They own MLB’s worst run differential (-122), mostly because of poor pitching. They have also dealt with other injuries, including Brent Rooker’s season-ending surgery.

With Langeliers out of the picture, other catchers who are trade candidates include Hunter Goodman (Colorado Rockies), Ryan Jeffers (Minnesota Twins) and Tyler Stephenson (Cincinnati Reds).
